cards.front: Recall a key point about Galaxies & Galaxy Types
cards.back: Galaxies are classified by shape: elliptical, spiral (barred and unbarred) and irregular

cards.front: Recall a key point about Galaxies & Galaxy Types
cards.back: The Hubble tuning-fork diagram classifies galaxies but does not represent an evolutionary sequence

cards.front: Recall a key point about Galaxies & Galaxy Types
cards.back: Elliptical galaxies range from nearly spherical (E0) to highly elongated (E7); they contain old stars and little gas/dust

cards.front: Recall a key point about Galaxies & Galaxy Types
cards.back: Spiral galaxies are labelled Sa–Sd (tight to loose arms) and barred spirals SBa–SBd

cards.front: Recall a key point about Galaxies & Galaxy Types
cards.back: Irregular galaxies (Irr) have no definite shape and often have active star formation

cards.front: Recall a key point about Galaxies & Galaxy Types
cards.back: The Local Group contains over 80 galaxies including the Milky Way and Andromeda (M31)

cards.front: What should you know about gcse astronomy exam tips — galaxies & galaxy types?
cards.back: 1. For Galaxies & Galaxy Types questions, define key terms before explaining processes 2. Use 'because' to link cause and effect in your explanations 3. Include units in all calculations and show your working for method marks 4. When evaluating Galaxies & Galaxy Types, consider both the quality of evidence and practical implications 5. For extended response questions, plan your answer: identify AO1/AO2/AO3 requirements first
